about.title: Duarte Car Accident Claims
about.longDescription: Duarte sees its share of collisions along the I-210 corridor and busy surface streets like Huntington Drive and Buena Vista Street, with reported crashes trending highest on Friday afternoons between 4 and 6 p.m. In a recent year, 69 injury collisions left 81 people hurt and resulted in one traffic death in this Los Angeles County community. When you're recovering from a wreck, dealing with insurance adjusters and mounting bills can feel overwhelming on top of the physical pain. LawProactive is a free service — not a law firm — that connects injured people with independent personal injury attorneys who work on contingency, meaning there's no fee unless you recover. We help you find someone who can evaluate your situation, explain your options under California law, and start protecting evidence before it disappears.

whyChoose.title: Why Talk to an Attorney Before the Insurer Calls

items.title: California's Clock Is Running
items.desc: You generally have two years from the crash date to file a personal injury claim in California, but that window can shrink to as little as six months if a government entity — like a city road crew or transit agency — is involved. Waiting too long can cost you the right to recover anything at all.

items.title: Comparative Fault Can Work Against You
items.desc: California uses pure comparative fault, meaning your compensation can be reduced by whatever percentage of blame gets assigned to you. Insurers often try to shift blame early, which is why it helps to have someone reviewing the facts before you say the wrong thing.

items.title: Recorded Statements Can Be Used Against You
items.desc: An adjuster who calls quickly may ask for a recorded statement — but anything you say can later be used to minimize your claim. Since California places no cap on non-economic damages like pain and suffering, it's worth talking to an attorney before you talk to the other side's insurer.

items.question: How long do I have to file a claim after a car accident in Duarte?
items.answer: Under California law, you typically have two years from the date of the crash to file a personal injury lawsuit. If your accident involved a government vehicle or a road hazard on a city-maintained street, that deadline could be as short as six months, so it's best to act quickly.

items.question: I was partly at fault for the crash on Huntington Drive — can I still recover anything?
items.answer: Possibly, yes. California follows pure comparative fault, which means you can still recover damages even if you were partially responsible, though your compensation would be reduced by your percentage of fault. An independent attorney can help evaluate how fault might be allocated in your specific situation.

items.question: Should I give a recorded statement to the other driver's insurance company?
items.answer: It's generally wise to avoid giving a recorded statement until you've spoken with an attorney, since insurers often use these statements to reduce or deny claims. Anything you say early on, even something that seems harmless, can be taken out of context later.
